common:
Use case ui-mockup. Create ONE final-quality page design in the SELECTED Mission Frontier visual system, shown by the attached reference. This is a SINGLE PAGE in one coherent complete product design set, NOT an alternative style or a collage. Target 1600 x 1024 desktop landscape, no browser/device chrome. Date anchor Sunday 6 September 2026 Pacific/Auckland. Tiny "Design study · sample data" marking. Agent Harness is the temporary product name.
The user has approved the attached strategy-game world, wants a NEW frontend, and explicitly discards the old dashboard UI. The actual game is the core UI: continuous beautifully rendered isometric colony, pale ceramic bases, slate roads, blue river, purple foliage, friendly robot workers. Project bases represent repositories; individual task crews can be selected and followed. Preserve these exact material, lighting, terrain and robot design choices across pages.
For this page, design a focused overlay or full workspace over that same world, as specified below. Use a wide restrained navy/teal glass tactical HUD with near-opaque reading surfaces, thin cool-grey borders, corners about 10px, warm white text, muted blue-grey secondary text, blue selected/primary actions, amber decisions, coral-red failure and muted green success. Background game world remains recognisable at edges. Do not recreate the old app shell or add a permanent sidebar outside the overlay. A small global title, project selector and "Return to world" / close affordance establish location; content has clear hierarchy and one dominant primary action. Practical UI controls must be plainly labelled, not hidden behind fantasy vocabulary.
Font Inter-like with 15–16px body and form controls, 12–13px metadata minimum, 24px titles; aligned tabular numerals; realistic line lengths. Prefer spacious grouped rows, separators and clear headings. No gratuitous KPI-card grids, neon, holographic microtext, decorative charts, paragraphs of exposition, cards nested in cards, duplicate controls or fake resource/XP bars. Never put multiple screen ideas in one image.
Core rules throughout the set: Task/Project/Agent/Skill labels remain familiar. Past/current/future stages visually distinct; future evidence is not invented. 10 stages remain Triage, Repo scouts, Grill, Task spec, Impl plan, Implement, Dev review, Test, Final review, Human approval; not all need be on every page. Running work continues while overlays are open. Current model policies are read-only for started runs; changes apply only to eligible future roles or new-task defaults. Default role examples Luna XHigh and Sol High. Dollar values called "Approx. cost" and supported by "API-rate estimate", never actual billed charge. Only sample data in the mock, no claims of live account health. No arbitrary speed-up, pause-all, drag-to-complete, automatic merge, or game animation presented as proof of work.
Existing service supports task summaries, retained activity/runs/artifacts, project add/list, model catalog/defaults/role policies, gated lifecycle commands and candidate-bound PR delivery. UX additions requested for the new product may be designed, but don't scatter backend implementation labels or TODOs in the product interface. Use precise user language and visually excellent fit with no clipping.
